description: Authorizes a completed result entry: sets result_entry.result_status to AUTHORIZED and cascades accession_tests.authorization_status to AUTHORIZED.
validation: resultEntryId must exist and belong to organization + branch
resultEntryId should be in COMPLETED status before authorization per the intended workflow - see database_gap note

errors.condition: resultEntryId does not reference an existing result entry
resultEntryId is not in COMPLETED status

response.error: Result entry must be completed before authorization

relationships: result_authorization.result_entry_id -> result_entry.id (unused by current e2e flow)
constraints: result_status NOT NULL CHECK IN (PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, AUTHORIZED, REJECTED) - no state-machine CHECK enforcing COMPLETED before AUTHORIZED

notes: database/schema/021_result_authorization.sql defines a dedicated result_authorization table (with its own authorization_status, authorized_at, authorized_by, rejection_reason columns), but database/e2e-validation/011_result_authorization.sql does not use that table at all - it authorizes directly via result_entry.result_status and accession_tests.authorization_status. This contract documents the behavior actually exercised by the e2e flow; the result_authorization table itself currently has no e2e-validation or api_contracts_test coverage and appears to be an unused/future table - worth confirming with the team whether authorization should be tracked there instead. Separately, result_entry.result_status has no CHECK/trigger enforcing that a row must be COMPLETED before it can move to AUTHORIZED, so database/api_contracts_test/019_result_authorization.sql's out-of-order authorization scenario (API-T158) is a confirmed DB GAP - the 400 response reflects intended API-layer business logic, not a DB-enforced rule.
